passages: [prose] The study was carried out on old secondary or natural broad-leaved forests in the Shiiba Research Forest, Kyushu University (3221 0 N, 13105 0 E), the Kashiba National Forest (3221 0 N, 13112 0 E), and the Tano Forest Science Station, Miyazaki University (3151 0 N, 13117 0 E) in the Kyushu Central Mountains (Figure 1). We selected 11 sites at different elevations from 177 m above sea level (a.s.l.) to 1604 m a.s.l. in these areas (Table 1). The Tano forest (177 m a.s.l.) included evergreen broad-leaved trees such as Castanopsis sieboldii and C. cuspidata. The Kashiba forest (723, 787 m a.s.l.) included evergreen broad-leaved trees such as Quercus acta and Q. salicina. In the Shiiba forest (1068, 1095, 1187, 1209, 1249, 1410, 1483, and 1604 m a.s.l.), there are deciduous broad-leaved trees, such as Fagus crenata, Q. crispula, Acer sieboldianum, and Ac. pictum, and coniferous trees, including Abies firma. There is little understory vegetation (such as herbs, which are pollen resources) due to overgrazing by deer in Kashiba and Shiiba. The annual mean temperature was 17.2C at 177 m a.s.l. in Tano from 2001 to 2017, and it was 8.5C at 1604 m a.s.l. in Shiiba from 2016 to 2017. The mean

[prose] Yellow pan traps were used for the sample collection (Figure 2). Pan traps have low human bias and are the most efficient and cost-effective methods for large-scale and longterm monitoring schemes with surveyors of different experience levels for all insect groups (Westphal et al., 2008). One limitation is that color preference differs depending on the species for all insect groups (Leong & Thorp, 1999), so that species that favor other colors may be under-sampled and their numbers underestimated. A yellow plastic bowl with a diameter of 15 cm was used. Each bowl was filled with approximately 150 ml of water with a few drops of dishwashing detergent as a surfactant.

[prose] We selected five functional traits that were expected to respond to elevational changes (body size, trophic level, feeding guild, flight duration, and elevational range) (Table S1). Body size was taken from the literature data of Tadauchi and Murao (2014) (for bees) and Terayama and Suda (2016) (for wasps). Trophic levels were defined at three levels: (1) herbivores (pollinator bees), (2) primary predators (predators and parasitoids of herbivores), and (3) secondary predators (predators and parasitoids of predators). Feeding guild was divided into four types that were classified according to the mechanism that adults use to feed their larvae: pollination, hunting, brood parasitism, and parasitoidism. The flight duration was calculated as the number of sampling times that the species was collected. The elevational range was calculated as the difference between the highest and lowest elevations at which the species was collected.

[prose] Increases in FD of several traits at high elevations indicate that species adopt different strategies and functional traits to coexist. Our research site on Kyushu Island has a warm, humid environment, with an annual mean temperature of $8 . 5 ^ { \circ } \mathbf { C }$ at the highest elevation (1604 m a.s.l.). Because physical stresses on Aculeata communities at our sites are mild, SD might not decrease at high elevations as a result.

[prose] In total, we collected 918 Aculeata individuals, including 298 in spring, 289 in summer, and 331 in autumn, and 107 species, including 41 Apoidea, 39 Vespoidea, and 27 Chrysidoidea (Table S2). The most abundant species was Anoplius pacificus (58 individuals). Bischoffitilla ardescens, which was collected at 177–1483 m a.s.l., had the largest elevational range. In contrast, Auplopus kyotensis was only collected at 177 m a.s.l. and Anteon jurineanum, A. insertum, and Lasioglossum zunaga were only collected at 1604 m a.s.l. Species composition was “turnover” along the elevational distance (Table S3).

[prose] We also considered species distribution bias in the study. Since southern species are warm-adapted species, they are expected to be abundant in the lowlands. Since northern species are cool-adapted species, they are expected to be abundant in the highlands. We expected SD to increase when the elevational distributions of the southern and northern species overlapped. To analyze species distribution bias, we defined the distribution index of the species. The Japanese archipelago is divided into seven areas and numbered in order from the north: (1) North of Hokkaido, (2) Hokkaido, (3) East Honshu,

[prose] (4) West Honshu and Shikoku; (5) Kyushu (including Osumi Island), (6) Amami Island and Okinawa Island, (7) Yaeyama Island and the Oriental region (Table S1). The average value in the area where a certain species was distributed was used as the species distribution index. For example, the distribution index of species distributed in Hokkaido and East Honshu was 2.5. The more southward the distribution of the species, the larger the distribution index. Distribution information for species was obtained from data from Tadauchi and Murao (2014), and Terayama and Suda (2016). An index of morphological species without a distribution record was applied in region 5 (Kyushu).

[prose] The two different dissimilarities in species composition were examined to determine whether the change in species composition was “nestedness” or “turnover,” according to the difference in elevation. We partitioned the Bray-Curtis index into “nestedness” (abundance gradient, according to the explanation in the software), and “turnover” (balanced variation) components, using the R package “betapart” (Baselga et al., 2018). The distance decay of similarity was tested using the mantel test calculated using the R package “vegan” (Oksanen et al., 2018), and “ecodist” (Goslee et al., 2020). All statistical analyses were performed using R version 3.5.0, for Windows (R Core Team, 2018).

[prose] SD based on Simpson's index showed a significant linear increase with increasing elevation (Figure 3; $r = 0 . 8 0 0 , p = 0 . 0 0 2 )$ . Species richness also increased with elevation (Figure 4; r = 0.663, p = 0.015).
